findings.title: The customer-visible hero headline is not reachable from the Visual Editor on this template
findings.measured: On the served home page's visible text, the SOURCE sentence "The product development system for teams and agents" appears 4 times (two painted layers x two viewports) and the operator's authored value appears 2 times (the 1x1 accessible copy, once per viewport).
findings.mechanism: home.main.hero.headline has exactly TWO bindings, both on node n000089, which computes to 1x1 px (a screen-reader copy). The sentence a visitor reads is painted by n000084 + n000087 inside an aria-hidden wrapper, and by a per-word split (n000070/74/78/82) — none of which carries any slot binding. Measured live in Chromium: n000089 w=1 h=1; n000084 w=703 h=64; n000087 w=784 h=64. Clicking either painted span in the editor returns `no slot binds this element`; the node that DOES bind cannot be clicked at all (`Element is outside of the viewport`).
findings.whyTheTwinCoBinderMissedIt: the template's paint-twin co-binder produced 4 paint-twin bindings on this whole lineage (manifest counts.paintTwinBindings=4 of 9,929) — it co-binds a twin whose TEXT matches, and the painted headline is split across two spans so no single node's text equals the sentence.
findings.consequence: a gate reading `authored visual-editor values missing from output = 0` is TRUE and simultaneously the visitor still reads the source's headline. That is exactly the shape of a manufactured zero, which is why it is asserted with its real number in the suite (28.P11.11) instead of being mentioned in prose.
findings.notFixedBecause: the Recon Template is IMMUTABLE and Exact Reconstruction is FROZEN by this task's contract; fixing it means changing the Slot V2 compiler's twin co-binding and recompiling the template, which is out of this phase's ownership.
findings.suggestedOwner: Slot V2 / twin-binding (src/recon-template/twin-binding.ts) — co-bind a CONTIGUOUS RUN of sibling text nodes whose concatenation matches a bound node's text, not just a single node.

findings.title: A release BUILD refused every Visual Editor edit on a review-flagged slot — FOUND AND FIXED
findings.measured: The first real `release:build` of this canary FAILED at the content stage with 3 `review-slot-not-writable` errors — home.main.hero.headline, home.main.cta.new-loops.label.02, home.main.cta.new-loops.href — the exact three edits the journey had just made and the editor had previewed happily. With the whole operator brand pass in place the same defect reproduces at 124 errors (failure-injection proof #4).
findings.rootCause: `prepareContentRun` was called by the content stage runner without any review opt-in, so `buildContentUnits` left every review-flagged slot out of the units, and `validateGenerationResult` correctly rejected values written for keys outside the units. §11 says a review slot is never AUTO-written; it does not say an operator cannot decide one, and the Visual Editor exists for exactly that.
findings.fix: a PER-KEY opt-in. `buildContentUnits` takes `operatorReviewSlotKeys`; `prepareContentRun` narrows the caller's list to review slots that are actually in scope for the run and RECORDS it on the run manifest (`operatorReviewSlotKeys`); the content stage runner derives it from authored.slotValues ∪ routeContent ∪ urls. The blanket `includeReview` flag stays OFF, so nothing widens beyond the named keys, and a key that leaves the scope with a disabled route is excluded.
findings.whyNotIncludeReview:true: that would pull all 1,493 review-flagged slots on this template into generation scope and change what every future generator may write. Measured on this canary: 124 keys opted in, includeReview still false.
findings.invariantPreserved: an opted-in key moves from `reviewSlotKeys` into `units`; `inScopeSlotKeys()` is their UNION, so the accounting denominator is unchanged — re-measured: inScopeSlots=3,079, reconciled=true, templateCoverage.complete=true.
